newsitem.title: USA: Coffee still rising, Starbucks hikes prices again.
newsitem.headline: Coffee still rising, Starbucks hikes prices again.

text.p: The price of coffee, after reaching a 20-year high earlier this week, leaped again on the free-wheeling futures market Wednesday, prompting upscale coffee retailer Starbucks Corp. to raise prices again.
On New York's Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, coffee for July delivery jumped 21.25 cents to about $2.96 a pound, the highest in two decades.
The rise has been fuelled by jitters about cold weather in Brazil at a time when coffee inventories are already low and supply is tight from Latin America.

Roasters have been passing on the higher cost of coffee, and Starbucks said it will raise prices for drip coffee by five cents a cup and for espresso beverages by 10 cents a cup, effective Friday at its approximately 1,100 stores.
Starbucks also said it will raise the price of whole bean coffee by 40 cents a pound.
"Tighter supplies and increased demand for coffee have been causing prices to continue to rise worldwide," Starbucks said in a statement.
"Even though we are taking a price increase, we are only taking the minimal increase to offset these higher costs," the company said.
The increase is the second time Seattle-based Starbucks has raised prices this year. In March, it added five cents to the price of a cup and bean prices went up 30 cents a pound.
Last week, Maxwell House Coffee Co., a unit of Philip Morris Cos. Inc., and Procter & Gamble Co.'s Folger Coffee Co. also boosted their prices.

Forecasts for cool winter weather in Brazil, the biggest exporter, did not point to a damaging frost. But they were enough to trigger new buying in a rally that has lifted prices for high-quality arabica coffees by 150 percent since the start of the year.

"Coffee is physically tight with stockpiles in both consumer and producer countries at 20-year lows, and this makes the market extremely prone to weather scares in Brazil," said the brokerage house GNI Ltd.
According to the latest reports, cooler-than-normal weather is expected in Brazil's coffee belt this week but no damaging cold was forecast.
